items.title: For a flat ring map and a finite ideal the gluing category is abelian and the canonical functor is exact and commutes with colimits
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma works with the gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t) attached to a flat ring map varphi : R -> S and the ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_t) of R, and asserts that this category is abelian and that the canonical functor Can is exact and preserves arbitrary colimits (source lines 24742-24748). The proof has to work with an object of that category, namely a tuple (M', M_i, alpha_i, alpha_ij) consisting of an S-module, R_{f_i}-modules and gluing data, and to show that kernels and cokernels can be formed componentwise as Ker(varphi') and Ker(varphi_i), respectively, with the gluing maps induced (proof lines 24751-24760). The key point is that this componentwise construction is legitimate precisely because R -> S is flat, so that taking kernels and cokernels commutes with - tensor_R S (proof lines 24761-24762); exactness is then reduced to the R-flatness of the localizations R_{f_i} and of S, and commutation with colimits to the corresponding property of tensor products (proof lines 24763-24764).
